claim: Tryparedoxin peroxidases are distant relatives of glutathione peroxidase 4 in higher eukaryotes.
source: Tryparedoxin peroxidases, distant relatives of glutathione peroxidase 4 in higher eukaryotes, are responsible for the detoxification of lipid-derived hydroperoxides in African trypanosomes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a characterization of tryparedoxin peroxidases and their relationship to GPx4.

claim: Tryparedoxin peroxidases are responsible for the detoxification of lipid-derived hydroperoxides in African trypanosomes.
source: Tryparedoxin peroxidases, distant relatives of glutathione peroxidase 4 in higher eukaryotes, are responsible for the detoxification of lipid-derived hydroperoxides in African trypanosomes.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the function of tryparedoxin peroxidases supported by the experimental work in the manuscript.

claim: The lethal phenotype of procyclic Trypanosoma brucei that lack tryparedoxin peroxidases fulfils all criteria defining ferroptosis.
source: The lethal phenotype of procyclic Trypanosoma brucei that lack the enzymes fulfils all criteria defining a form of regulated cell death termed ferroptosis.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experimental observations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Viability of peroxidase-deficient parasites is preserved by α-tocopherol.
source: Viability of the parasites is preserved by α-tocopherol, ferrostatin-1, liproxstatin-1 and deferoxamine.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Viability of peroxidase-deficient parasites is preserved by ferrostatin-1.
source: Viability of the parasites is preserved by α-tocopherol, ferrostatin-1, liproxstatin-1 and deferoxamine.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Viability of peroxidase-deficient parasites is preserved by liproxstatin-1.
source: Viability of the parasites is preserved by α-tocopherol, ferrostatin-1, liproxstatin-1 and deferoxamine.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Viability of peroxidase-deficient parasites is preserved by deferoxamine.
source: Viability of the parasites is preserved by α-tocopherol, ferrostatin-1, liproxstatin-1 and deferoxamine.
evidence: This is directly stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Peroxidase-deficient cells display primarily mitochondrial lipid peroxidation without protecting agent.
source: Without protecting agent, the cells display, primarily mitochondrial, lipid peroxidation, loss of the mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 1C and Figure 6.

claim: Peroxidase-deficient cells display loss of the mitochondrial membrane potential without protecting agent.
source: Without protecting agent, the cells display, primarily mitochondrial, lipid peroxidation, loss of the mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Peroxidase-deficient cells display ATP depletion without protecting agent.
source: Without protecting agent, the cells display, primarily mitochondrial, lipid peroxidation, loss of the mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Sensors for mitochondrial oxidants attenuate the cell death of peroxidase-deficient parasites.
source: Sensors for mitochondrial oxidants and chelatable iron as well as overexpression of a mitochondrial iron-superoxide dismutase attenuate the cell death.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4 showing MitoSOX protection.

claim: Sensors for chelatable iron attenuate the cell death of peroxidase-deficient parasites.
source: Sensors for mitochondrial oxidants and chelatable iron as well as overexpression of a mitochondrial iron-superoxide dismutase attenuate the cell death.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 8 showing RPA protection.

claim: Overexpression of a mitochondrial iron-superoxide dismutase attenuates the cell death of peroxidase-deficient parasites.
source: Sensors for mitochondrial oxidants and chelatable iron as well as overexpression of a mitochondrial iron-superoxide dismutase attenuate the cell death.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Electron microscopy revealed mitochondrial matrix condensation in peroxidase-deficient parasites.
source: Electron microscopy revealed mitochondrial matrix condensation and enlarged cristae.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 3.

claim: Electron microscopy revealed enlarged cristae in peroxidase-deficient parasites.
source: Electron microscopy revealed mitochondrial matrix condensation and enlarged cristae.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by electron microscopy images in Figure 3.

claim: The peroxidase-deficient parasites are subject to lethal iron-induced lipid peroxidation that probably originates at the inner mitochondrial membrane.
source: The peroxidase-deficient parasites are subject to lethal iron-induced lipid peroxidation that probably originates at the inner mitochondrial membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing mitochondrial-specific lipid peroxidation in Figure 6.

claim: Ferroptosis is an ancient cell death program.
source: Taken together, ferroptosis is an ancient cell death program that can occur at individual subcellular membranes and is counterbalanced by evolutionary distant thiol peroxidases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that ferroptosis occurs in trypanosomes, which are early-branching eukaryotes.

claim: Ferroptosis can occur at individual subcellular membranes.
source: Taken together, ferroptosis is an ancient cell death program that can occur at individual subcellular membranes and is counterbalanced by evolutionary distant thiol peroxidases.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that ferroptosis in trypanosomes appears to initiate specifically at the mitochondrial membrane.

claim: Ferroptosis is counterbalanced by evolutionary distant thiol peroxidases.
source: Taken together, ferroptosis is an ancient cell death program that can occur at individual subcellular membranes and is counterbalanced by evolutionary distant thiol peroxidases.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the finding that tryparedoxin peroxidases, which are distant relatives of GPx4, prevent ferroptosis in trypanosomes.

claim: Ferroptosis is characterized by the iron-dependent accumulation of cellular lipid hydroperoxides to lethal levels.
source: Ferroptosis is characterized by the iron-dependent accumulation of cellular lipid hydroperoxides to lethal levels.
evidence: This is a definition of ferroptosis cited from the literature.

claim: Ferroptosis has been implicated in the pathology of degenerative diseases.
source: This form of regulated cell death has been implicated in the pathology of degenerative diseases (e.g. Alzheimer's, Huntington's and Parkinson's diseases), cancer, ischemia-reperfusion injury and kidney degeneration (for recent reviews see [Doll and Conrad, 2017; Stockwell et al., 2017; Galluzzi et al., 2018]).
evidence: This is cited from review articles on ferroptosis.

claim: Ferroptosis has been implicated in cancer.
source: This form of regulated cell death has been implicated in the pathology of degenerative diseases (e.g. Alzheimer's, Huntington's and Parkinson's diseases), cancer, ischemia-reperfusion injury and kidney degeneration (for recent reviews see [Doll and Conrad, 2017; Stockwell et al., 2017; Galluzzi et al., 2018]).
evidence: This is cited from review articles on ferroptosis.

claim: Ferroptosis has been implicated in ischemia-reperfusion injury.
source: This form of regulated cell death has been implicated in the pathology of degenerative diseases (e.g. Alzheimer's, Huntington's and Parkinson's diseases), cancer, ischemia-reperfusion injury and kidney degeneration (for recent reviews see [Doll and Conrad, 2017; Stockwell et al., 2017; Galluzzi et al., 2018]).
evidence: This is cited from review articles on ferroptosis.

claim: Ferroptosis has been implicated in kidney degeneration.
source: This form of regulated cell death has been implicated in the pathology of degenerative diseases (e.g. Alzheimer's, Huntington's and Parkinson's diseases), cancer, ischemia-reperfusion injury and kidney degeneration (for recent reviews see [Doll and Conrad, 2017; Stockwell et al., 2017; Galluzzi et al., 2018]).
evidence: This is cited from review articles on ferroptosis.

claim: The term ferroptosis was coined in 2012 to describe a form of death in cancer cells induced by the small molecule erastin.
source: The term ferroptosis was coined in 2012 to describe a form of death in cancer cells induced by the small molecule erastin (Dixon et al., 2012; Dixon et al., 2014; Cao and Dixon, 2016).
evidence: This is a historical fact cited from the literature.

claim: Erastin inhibits glutathione biosynthesis and thus GPx4 activity.
source: Consequence is an inhibition of glutathione biosynthesis and thus of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPx4) activity.
evidence: This is a mechanistic explanation of how erastin induces ferroptosis, based on cited literature.

claim: GPx4 is the only glutathione peroxidase in mammalian cells that is able to detoxify lipid hydroperoxides even within membranes.
source: Of the eight glutathione peroxidases in mammalian cells, GPx4 is the only one that is able to detoxify lipid hydroperoxides even within membranes (Thomas et al., 1990; Seiler et al., 2008; Brigelius-Flohé and Maiorino, 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about GPx4 function cited from the literature.

claim: Inactivation of GPx4 by RSL3 induces ferroptosis.
source: Inactivation of GPx4 by chemicals like for example RSL3 induces ferroptosis (Yang et al., 2014)
evidence: This is cited from the literature on ferroptosis induction.

claim: Inducible GPx4-deletion in mice revealed that ferroptosis is a pervasive and dynamic form of cell death also in non-transformed cells.
source: and inducible GPx4-deletion in mice revealed that ferroptosis is a pervasive and dynamic form of cell death also in non-transformed cells (Friedmann Angeli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from a study on GPx4 deletion in mice.

claim: Heat-stressed plants can undergo a ferroptosis-like cell death.
source: Heat-stressed plants can also undergo a ferroptosis-like cell death (Distéfano et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from a study on plant cell death.

claim: A hallmark of ferroptosis is its suppression by iron chelators.
source: A hallmark of a cell death occurring exclusively by ferroptosis is its suppression by iron chelators (Dixon et al., 2012)
evidence: This is a defining characteristic of ferroptosis cited from the literature.

claim: A hallmark of ferroptosis is its suppression by lipophilic antioxidants.
source: or lipophilic antioxidants (Seiler et al., 2008; Krainz et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a defining characteristic of ferroptosis cited from the literature.

claim: A hallmark of ferroptosis is its suppression by the depletion of polyunsaturated fatty acids in membrane lipids.
source: as well as by the depletion of polyunsaturated fatty acids in membrane lipids (Doll et al., 2017; Kagan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a defining characteristic of ferroptosis cited from the literature.

claim: African trypanosomes are the causative agents of human sleeping sickness.
source: African trypanosomes (Trypanosoma brucei species) are the causative agents of human sleeping sickness and Nagana cattle disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge about African trypanosomes.

claim: African trypanosomes are the causative agents of Nagana cattle disease.
source: African trypanosomes (Trypanosoma brucei species) are the causative agents of human sleeping sickness and Nagana cattle disease.
evidence: This is established knowledge about African trypanosomes.

claim: Bloodstream form T. brucei rely exclusively on glycolysis for energy supply.
source: BS T. brucei rely exclusively on glycolysis for energy supply and have an only rudimentary mitochondrion
evidence: This is established knowledge about the metabolism of bloodstream form trypanosomes.

claim: Bloodstream form T. brucei have a rudimentary mitochondrion.
source: BS T. brucei rely exclusively on glycolysis for energy supply and have an only rudimentary mitochondrion
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mitochondrial structure in bloodstream form trypanosomes.

claim: In the procyclic stage, the single mitochondrion of T. brucei is fully elaborated.
source: whereas in the PC stage, the single mitochondrion is fully elaborated and the parasites gain ATP via oxidative phosphorylation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mitochondrial structure in procyclic form trypanosomes.

claim: Procyclic T. brucei gain ATP via oxidative phosphorylation.
source: whereas in the PC stage, the single mitochondrion is fully elaborated and the parasites gain ATP via oxidative phosphorylation.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the metabolism of procyclic form trypanosomes.

claim: Trypanosomes have an unusual thiol redox metabolism that is based on trypanothione and trypanothione reductase.
source: Trypanosomes have an unusual thiol redox metabolism that is based on trypanothione [N1, N8-bis(glutathionyl)spermidine, T(SH)2)] and the flavoenzyme trypanothione reductase (TR) (Krauth-Siegel and Leroux, 2012; Manta et al., 2013; Manta et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about trypanosome biochemistry cited from the literature.

claim: The trypanothione system delivers the reducing equivalents for a variety of crucial pathways.
source: The trypanothione system delivers the reducing equivalents for a variety of crucial pathways.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of the trypanothione system.

claim: Most reactions of the trypanothione system are mediated by tryparedoxin.
source: Most of the reactions are mediated by tryparedoxin (Tpx), an essential distant member of the thioredoxin protein family (Comini et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on trypanosome redox metabolism.

claim: Tryparedoxin is an essential distant member of the thioredoxin protein family.
source: Most of the reactions are mediated by tryparedoxin (Tpx), an essential distant member of the thioredoxin protein family (Comini et al., 2007).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on tryparedoxin.

claim: Trypanosomes lack catalase.
source: Trypanosomes lack catalase.
evidence: This is established knowledge about trypanosome antioxidant systems.

claim: Hydroperoxides in trypanosomes are detoxified by 2-Cys-peroxiredoxins.
source: Hydroperoxides are detoxified by 2-Cys-peroxiredoxins (Tetaud et al., 2001; Budde et al., 2003; Wilkinson et al., 2003) and non-selenium glutathione peroxidase-type (Px) enzymes (Hillebrand et al., 2003; Wilkinson et al., 2003; Schlecker et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on trypanosome peroxidases.

claim: Hydroperoxides in trypanosomes are detoxified by non-selenium glutathione peroxidase-type enzymes.
source: Hydroperoxides are detoxified by 2-Cys-peroxiredoxins (Tetaud et al., 2001; Budde et al., 2003; Wilkinson et al., 2003) and non-selenium glutathione peroxidase-type (Px) enzymes (Hillebrand et al., 2003; Wilkinson et al., 2003; Schlecker et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on trypanosome peroxidases.

claim: Peroxiredoxins in trypanosomes use hydrogen peroxide and peroxynitrite as main substrates.
source: Whereas the peroxiredoxins use hydrogen peroxide and peroxynitrite as main substrates (Thomson et al., 2003; Trujillo et al., 2004)
evidence: This is cited from the literature on peroxiredoxin substrate specificity.

claim: The Px-type enzymes in trypanosomes preferably detoxify lipid-derived hydroperoxides.
source: the Px-type enzymes preferably detoxify lipid-derived hydroperoxides (Diechtierow and Krauth-Siegel, 2011).
evidence: This is cited from previous work on Px-type enzyme substrate specificity.

claim: With NADPH as ultimate electron donor, the reducing equivalents flow via TR, T(SH)2, and tryparedoxin onto the peroxidases.
source: With NADPH as ultimate electron donor, the reducing equivalents flow via TR, T(SH)2, and tryparedoxin onto the peroxidases which therefore have been named tryparedoxin peroxidases (Castro and Tomás, 2008; Krauth-Siegel and Comini, 2008; Krauth-Siegel and Leroux, 2012; Manta et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on the trypanosome peroxidase cascade.

claim: Tandemly arranged genes encode three virtually identical Px-type enzymes (Px I, II, and III) in T. brucei.
source: Tandemly arranged genes encode three virtually identical Px-type enzymes (Px I, II, and III) in T. brucei (Hillebrand et al., 2003).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on T. brucei peroxidases.

claim: RNA-interference against the Px-type enzymes results in a severe growth defect in both BS and PC T. brucei.
source: RNA-interference against the Px-type enzymes results in a severe growth defect in both BS and PC T. brucei (Wilkinson et al., 2003; Schlecker et al., 2005).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on RNAi studies of Px enzymes.

claim: Proliferation of Px-depleted BS parasites can be restored by supplementing the medium with Trolox.
source: Proliferation of the Px-depleted BS parasites can, however, be restored by supplementing the medium with the vitamin E-analog Trolox [(±)−6-hydroxy-2,5,7,8-tetramethylchromane-2-carboxylic acid] (Diechtierow and Krauth-Siegel, 2011).
evidence: This is cited from previous work on Px-depleted parasites.

claim: Cells lacking GPx4 can be rescued by Trolox.
source: The same is true for cells lacking GPx4, the closest related enzyme in mammals (Seiler et al., 2008).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on GPx4-deficient cells.

claim: Selective knockout of the gene encoding the mitochondrial Px III has only a mild and transient effect on the in vitro proliferation of BS T. brucei.
source: Selective knockout (KO) of the gene encoding the mitochondrial Px III has only a mild and transient effect on the in vitro proliferation of BS T. brucei and the mutant parasites are fully infectious in the mouse model.
evidence: This is cited from previous work on Px III knockout.

claim: Px III knockout mutant parasites are fully infectious in the mouse model.
source: Selective knockout (KO) of the gene encoding the mitochondrial Px III has only a mild and transient effect on the in vitro proliferation of BS T. brucei and the mutant parasites are fully infectious in the mouse model.
evidence: This is cited from previous work on Px III knockout.

claim: Cells that lack the cytosolic peroxidases Px I and II die after transfer into Trolox-free medium.
source: In contrast, cells that lack the cytosolic peroxidases Px I and II die after transfer into Trolox-free medium (Diechtierow and Krauth-Siegel, 2011; Hiller et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from previous work on Px I and II knockout.

claim: The lethal phenotype of BS parasites lacking Px I and II starts at the lysosome.
source: The lethal phenotype of the BS parasites starts at the lysosome and is closely linked to the endocytosis of iron-loaded host transferrin (Hiller et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from previous work on the mechanism of cell death in Px I/II knockout BS parasites.

claim: The lethal phenotype of BS parasites lacking Px I and II is closely linked to the endocytosis of iron-loaded host transferrin.
source: The lethal phenotype of the BS parasites starts at the lysosome and is closely linked to the endocytosis of iron-loaded host transferrin (Hiller et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from previous work on the mechanism of cell death in Px I/II knockout BS parasites.

claim: In PC T. brucei, the presence of either the cytosolic or the mitochondrial peroxidases is sufficient for viability.
source: In the PC insect stage of T. brucei, the presence of either the cytosolic or the mitochondrial peroxidases is sufficient for viability.
evidence: This is cited from previous work on PC T. brucei peroxidases.

claim: Deletion of the complete peroxidase (px I-III) locus is lethal in PC T. brucei.
source: However, deletion of the complete peroxidase (px I-III) locus is lethal.
evidence: This is cited from previous work on PC T. brucei peroxidases.

claim: The cell death of PC Px I-III knockout parasites can be reverted by exogenous Trolox.
source: The cell death can be reverted by exogenous Trolox, deferoxamine (Dfx) or MitoQ which suggested an iron-induced lipid peroxidation that may start at the mitochondrion (Schaffroth et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from previous work on PC Px I-III knockout parasites.

claim: The cell death of PC Px I-III knockout parasites can be reverted by deferoxamine.
source: The cell death can be reverted by exogenous Trolox, deferoxamine (Dfx) or MitoQ which suggested an iron-induced lipid peroxidation that may start at the mitochondrion (Schaffroth et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from previous work on PC Px I-III knockout parasites.

claim: The cell death of PC Px I-III knockout parasites can be reverted by MitoQ.
source: The cell death can be reverted by exogenous Trolox, deferoxamine (Dfx) or MitoQ which suggested an iron-induced lipid peroxidation that may start at the mitochondrion (Schaffroth et al., 2016).
evidence: This is cited from previous work on PC Px I-III knockout parasites.

claim: The minimum concentration of Trolox to ensure full viability of the Px I-III KO cells is 50 µM.
source: The minimum concentration to ensure full viability of the Px I-III KO cells is 50 µM Trolox and 100 µM Dfx, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The minimum concentration of Dfx to ensure full viability of the Px I-III KO cells is 100 µM.
source: The minimum concentration to ensure full viability of the Px I-III KO cells is 50 µM Trolox and 100 µM Dfx, respectively.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: 10 µM Trolox and 20 µM Dfx alone are not sufficient to protect Px I-III KO cells but in combination restore cell viability.
source: 10 µM Trolox and 20 µM Dfx alone are not sufficient but in combination, restore cell viability (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Partial complexation of iron by Dfx lowers the concentration of Trolox that is required to protect the cells.
source: Evidently, partial complexation of iron by Dfx lowers the concentration of Trolox that is required to protect the cells.
evidence: This is an inference based on the synergistic effect of Trolox and Dfx.

claim: Free iron ions react with hydroperoxides generating highly deleterious alkoxy radicals.
source: The concerted action of Dfx and Trolox is probably related to the fact that free iron ions react with hydroperoxides generating highly deleterious alkoxy radicals.
evidence: This is established knowledge about iron-catalyzed reactions.

claim: Trolox is a more powerful scavenger of alkoxy radicals compared to peroxy radicals.
source: As shown recently, Trolox is a more powerful scavenger of alkoxy radicals compared to peroxy radicals (Alberto et al., 2013).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on Trolox reactivity.

claim: At 1 µM, α-Tocopherol fully reverts the lethal phenotype of mammalian cells lacking GPx4.
source: At 1 µM, α-Tocopherol (α-Toc) fully reverts the lethal phenotype of mammalian cells lacking GPx4 (Seiler et al., 2008).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on GPx4-deficient cells.

claim: 100 µM α-Toc was not sufficient to fully prevent cell lysis of Px I-III KO cells.
source: Unexpectedly, even 100 µM α-Toc was not sufficient to fully prevent cell lysis.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Px I-III KO cells pre-loaded with 10 µM α-Toc slightly proliferated within the 6 hr observation time even in the absence of further exogenous α-Toc.
source: In a second approach, the cells were pre-loaded with 10 µM α-Toc in the presence of 100 µM Trolox and then transferred into Trolox-free medium ± α-Toc. In this case, the Px I-III KO cells even slightly proliferated within the 6 hr observation time, remarkably also in the absence of further exogenous α-Toc.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Uptake of α-Toc by the parasites is slow compared to Trolox.
source: Apparently, uptake of α-Toc by the parasites is slow compared to Trolox, but after proper incorporation, indeed α-Toc is the superior protecting agent.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that pre-loading with α-Toc is more effective than direct addition.

claim: After proper incorporation, α-Toc is the superior protecting agent compared to Trolox.
source: Apparently, uptake of α-Toc by the parasites is slow compared to Trolox, but after proper incorporation, indeed α-Toc is the superior protecting agent.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that pre-loaded α-Toc provides better protection.

claim: An analog of α-Toc in which the isoprenoid side chain is truncated to a methyl group is an even better antioxidant than α-Toc.
source: As reported recently, an analog in which the isoprenoid side chain is truncated to a methyl group proved to be an even better antioxidant than α-Toc (Zilka et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on α-Toc analogs.

claim: 100 nM Fer-1 completely abolished the lethality of the Px I-III KO cells.
source: Indeed also in trypanosomes, 100 nM Fer-1 or 200 nM Lpx-1 completely abolished the lethality of the Px I-III KO cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A.

claim: 200 nM Lpx-1 completely abolished the lethality of the Px I-III KO cells.
source: Indeed also in trypanosomes, 100 nM Fer-1 or 200 nM Lpx-1 completely abolished the lethality of the Px I-III KO cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1A.

claim: Fer-1 and Lpx-1 act as radical-trapping agents which in phospholipid bilayers are significantly more potent antioxidants than α-Toc.
source: Mechanistically, the compounds act as radical-trapping agents which in phospholipid bilayers are significantly more potent antioxidants than α-Toc (Zilka et al., 2017).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on ferroptosis inhibitors.

claim: Mammalian ferroptotic cells show a time-dependent increase of both lipid and soluble reactive oxygen species production.
source: Mammalian ferroptotic cells show a time-dependent increase of both lipid and soluble reactive oxygen species (ROS) production (Dixon et al., 2012; Yang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on ferroptosis characteristics.

claim: After 2 hr in Trolox-free medium, DCF fluorescence was strongly increased in Px I-III KO cells indicating that the parasites are subject to general oxidative stress.
source: After 2 hr in Trolox-free medium, DCF fluorescence was strongly increased indicating that the parasites are subject to general oxidative stress (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1B.

claim: Px I-III KO parasites incubated for 2 hr in non-supplemented medium showed strong green BODIPY fluorescence indicating lipid peroxidation.
source: Cells that were kept for 2 hr in non-supplemented medium showed strong green fluorescence whereas cells incubated in the presence of the radical scavengers or iron chelator were protected from lipid peroxidation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: Cells incubated in the presence of radical scavengers or iron chelator were protected from lipid peroxidation.
source: Cells that were kept for 2 hr in non-supplemented medium showed strong green fluorescence whereas cells incubated in the presence of the radical scavengers or iron chelator were protected from lipid peroxidation (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by data in Figure 1C.

claim: RSL3 is a ferroptosis-inducing agent.
source: RSL3 (RAS-selective lethal) is a ferroptosis-inducing agent.
evidence: This is established knowledge about RSL3 cited from the literature.

claim: The (1S, 3R)-RSL3 isomer kills RAS-transformed tumorigenic fibroblast cell lines with EC50-values of 10 nM.
source: The (1S, 3R)-RSL3 isomer kills RAS-transformed tumorigenic fibroblast cell lines with EC50-values of 10 nM and irreversibly inactivates GPx4.
evidence: This is cited from the literature on RSL3 activity.

claim: The (1S, 3R)-RSL3 isomer irreversibly inactivates GPx4.
source: The (1S, 3R)-RSL3 isomer kills RAS-transformed tumorigenic fibroblast cell lines with EC50-values of 10 nM and irreversibly inactivates GPx4.
evidence: This is cited from the literature on RSL3 mechanism.

claim: The other three diastereomers of RSL3 display EC50-values of 2.5 to 5 µM.
source: The other three diastereomers display EC50-values of 2.5 to 5 µM (Yang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on RSL3 stereoisomers.

claim: After 24 and 48 hr, RSL3 showed EC50-values of 2 and 4 µM against BS T. brucei.
source: After 24 and 48 hr, EC50-values of 2 and 4 µM were obtained which increased about two-fold after 72 hr probably because of long-term instability of the compounds in the medium.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on experimental measurements.

claim: RSL3 EC50-values increased about two-fold after 72 hr probably because of long-term instability of the compounds in the medium.
source: After 24 and 48 hr, EC50-values of 2 and 4 µM were obtained which increased about two-fold after 72 hr probably because of long-term instability of the compounds in the medium.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the data.

claim: RSL3 was trypanocidal but selectivity for the (1S,3R)-isomer could not be detected.
source: Thus, RSL3 was trypanocidal but selectivity for the (1S,3R)-isomer could not be detected (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on experimental data.

claim: A lack of stereo-specificity and EC-values in the low micromolar range were reported for non-transformed fibroblast cell lines treated with RSL3.
source: A lack of stereo-specificity and EC-values in the low micromolar range were reported for non-transformed fibroblast cell lines as well (Yang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on RSL3 activity in different cell types.

claim: The EC50-values of RSL3 obtained in the presence or absence of radical-trapping antioxidants were virtually the same.
source: The EC50-values obtained in the presence or absence of the radical-trapping antioxidants were virtually the same which implies that the trypanocidal activity of RSL3 is not related to inhibition of the peroxidases.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on experimental data.

claim: The trypanocidal activity of RSL3 is not related to inhibition of the peroxidases.
source: The EC50-values obtained in the presence or absence of the radical-trapping antioxidants were virtually the same which implies that the trypanocidal activity of RSL3 is not related to inhibition of the peroxidases.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that antioxidants don't affect RSL3 EC50 values.

claim: Mammalian mouse embryonic fibroblasts in which authentic GPx4 is replaced by a Cys-mutant are much less sensitive towards (1S,3R)-RSL3 than the respective wildtype cells.
source: Mammalian mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEF and PFa1 cells) in which authentic GPx4 is replaced by a Cys-mutant are much less sensitive towards (1S,3R)-RSL3 than the respective wildtype cells (Ingold et al., 2018).
evidence: This is cited from the literature on GPx4 mutants and RSL3 sensitivity.

claim: RSL3 carries a chloroacetamido group.
source: RSL3 carries a chloroacetamido group.
evidence: This is a statement about the chemical structure of RSL3.

claim: Several compounds with a chloroacetamido substituent proved to be trypanocidal and to inactivate Tpx.
